title: A benchmark run records the worker branch's HEAD as its commit, which land's rebase rewrites, so the record names a commit that is not on main
goal: bench_core.Bench records as the run's commit the merge-base of HEAD and origin/main when HEAD's _tools and .claude trees equal that commit's, so the commit stays on main when land rebases the worker's branch; when the trees differ (the branch changes the tools the run measures) it records HEAD, as today, and says on stderr that the commit is the branch's and a rebase rewrites it

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
    clone = os.path.join(t, "clone")
    bindir = os.path.join(t, "bin")
    os.mkdir(bindir)
    open(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), "w").write("#!/bin/sh\necho 0.0.0\n")
    os.chmod(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), 0o755)
    env = dict(os.environ, PATH=bindir + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"])
    def git(*a):
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com", *a], cwd=clone, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", "--local", ".", clone], check=True)
    git("update-ref", "refs/remotes/origin/main", "HEAD")
    git("switch", "-q", "-c", "work/ST-x")
    git("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "worker commit that land rebases")
    code = "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import bench_core; print(bench_core.Bench(sys.argv[1], 1).commit)"
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code, os.path.join(t, "scratch")], cwd=clone, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=120)
    assert p.returncode == 0, ("Bench failed", p.stderr[-300:])
    commit = p.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]
    on_main = subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, "origin/main"], cwd=clone).returncode == 0
    assert on_main, ("the record's commit is not on origin/main", commit, "HEAD", git("rev-parse", "--short=7", "HEAD"))

notes: Retro finding of the drain: session-load record rows committed on a worker branch name the worker's HEAD (bench_core.Bench.__init__ takes git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD), which land's rebase rewrites, so ST-nejgzptp's check (a session-load record row names a commit that is not on this branch) failed after landing, three times: ST-6zg57xiu's land was refused twice, and ST-rodj5ltd's rows named cd23d59 and were repointed by hand to 1f6011b. The planning side (a check never names a literal hash) is ST-6aemb7j5; this is the tool side. The retro's other remedy, land repointing the rows of the record it rebases, is not chosen: it needs a rewrite of a committed csv inside land, where the merge-base needs none. The repro plants a clone with one commit past a planted origin/main and runs Bench on it with a fake claude on PATH (no model call).
